title: developer-flowbook-sdk-atomic-actions-and-resumable-sessions-prd-draft
summary: This PRD draft proposes an SDK-centric pattern (the 'Flowbook') for exposing atomic action primitives and resumable sessions over the Hosted API streaming surface. Purpose: improve developer ergonomics when combining long-running streaming generation with deterministic tool calls and resumption semantics for flaky networks or client restarts.
background_and_context: Teams commonly build workflows that combine multi-turn streaming generation, side-effecting tool calls (search, DB writes, external APIs), and requirement for resumability. Current streaming surfaces are optimized for low-latency text deltas but lack a small, ergonomic set of primitives that make tool-synthesis deterministic, allow safe client replay, and provide compact telemetry hooks for cost/latency attribution. This doc offers a minimal API/SDK pattern + server-side contract to make these flows practical for product teams.
problem_statement: 1) Developers struggle to coordinate tool calls and model output in the presence of partial responses and reconnects. 2) Partial/incremental frames can lead to duplicate tool executions or lost state on reconnect. 3) Observability and cost attribution are noisy when clients must stitch multiple ephemeral streams. 4) Current SDK surfaces force teams to build custom idempotency and resume layers.
user_personas: Product engineer integrating LLM-driven form-filling and external DB writes
Platform engineer embedding Hosted API calls into server-side event handlers with strict SLOs
Solutions engineer building reference integrations that must safely retry across flaky mobile networks
goals: Define an SDK-level contract for atomic actions (start/commit/abort) that prevents double-execution of tool effects
Provide a resumable session token and compact checkpoint frames so clients can reconnect without losing progress or causing side-effects
Keep runtime overhead minimal (single-digit percent latency impact on tail) and make server-side changes incremental
Surface structured output envelopes for typed tool results and clear telemetry hooks for cost and latency attribution
non_goals: Reworking the entire streaming wire protocol; this is an additive SDK pattern on top of current streaming frames
Guaranteeing globally exactly-once semantics for arbitrary external services (we will provide idempotency helpers, not external transaction guarantees)
Replacing existing client SDKs wholesale — initial rollout will be opt-in and additive
proposed_primitives_overview: 1) Session token: opaque resumable_id returned at stream start. 2) Atomic action envelope: action_id + lifecycle events (action:start, action:commit, action:abort). 3) Checkpoint frame: compact state pointer (checkpoint_id) emitted periodically by server containing model progress and last-committed action_ids. 4) Structured result envelope: typed payloads for tool outputs (tool_result, diagnostics, partial_text).
stream_frame_contracts: Frame types (flat JSON): 1) delta: incremental model text (streamed for UI). 2) action_request: model requests a tool call; includes action_id and spec. 3) action_commit / action_abort: client acknowledges. 4) checkpoint: server-sent compact summary: {checkpoint_id, last_committed_action_ids, resume_hint}. 5) meta: session lifecycle events. Frames are order-guaranteed within a connection; checkpoint establishes a durable progress marker acknowledged by server-side routing and optional durable logs.
server_semantics_and_idempotency: - Server treats an action_commit with an action_id as the canonical side-effect marker. - Action_ids are client-generated or server-assigned UUIDs; SDKs will generate RFC4122 v4 IDs by default. - Server persists last_committed_action_ids per resumable_id when emitting checkpoint. - On reconnect, server will not re-emit action_request frames for action_ids that are present in last_committed_action_ids. - For external tool side effects, SDKs will attach idempotency keys equal to action_id to recommended tool adapters (search index writes, webhook calls).
telemetry_and_observability: Add compact telemetry fields to frames and server events: session_origin (sdk|direct-api), resume_count, checkpoint_latency_ms, per-frame_token_delta. Console dashboards should show per-session cost and a heatmap of 'action failures' vs 'resume events'. Provide a lightweight event export (s3/kafka) with schema versioning. Emphasize that telemetry keys are small strings to keep bandwidth low.
security_and_privacy: - Resumable tokens are opaque, short-lived (default 1 hour) and optionally bound to API key or client identity (for private deployments). - Checkpoint payloads must not include PII; SDKs should support redaction rules. - Atomic action metadata must be signed by the client when cross-account rollouts are used (private deployments with trust boundaries).
compatibility_and_fallbacks: - For older clients that don't implement the Flowbook, server will continue to stream delta frames as before. - If resumption fails (stale checkpoint/expired token), server will fall back to a fresh stream and emit a 'resume_failed' meta frame. - Tool adapters will support at-least-once retries; recommendations and helper libraries to deduplicate on action_id will be provided.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal experiment): SDK-only opt-in, internal teams, manual dashboarding. Phase 1 (beta): public JS/Python SDK release, console opt-in toggle, 2-week canary on low-traffic customers. Phase 2 (GA): server-side defaults for new sessions, migration guides for existing customers and partner integrations.
success_metrics: Reduction in customer-reported duplicate-tool-executions by 90% for flows using atomic actions
Resume success rate > 99% within token lifetime
Median time-to-commit for actions < 120ms additional latency vs baseline streaming
Adoption: 20% of new streaming sessions created via SDK flow within 6 months of GA
open_questions: Checkpoint frequency: tradeoff between smaller resume windows and increased checkpoint write load. Default suggestion: every 5s or after every committed action (whichever happens first).
Should action_ids be server-assigned by default to avoid client-ID collisions in multi-proxy setups? (we prefer client-assigned + server-validation to keep SDK ergonomics)
How to surface debugging of mismatched action_ids between client and server in a way that's safe for end-users?
Authentication model for resumable tokens in dedicated/private deployments: should tokens be bound to VPC identity or to API key?
implementation_notes: Server: persist resumable session state to a low-latency store (primary: in-memory + write-behind to durable log). Checkpoint writes should be append-only with compaction. Router: when accepting a resume, use the checkpoint to prune already-fulfilled action_requests. SDKs: default to uuidv4 action ids, provide automatic idempotency header helpers for common adapters, expose a debug flag to emit detailed per-frame diagnostics to developer console (never in production telemetry by default).
security_considerations: Sign or HMAC resumable tokens in multi-tenant hosted mode; rotate signing keys; provide policy to short-circuit resumes on suspected token theft. Limit the number of resumptions per session to mitigate replay attacks. Document recommended redaction and PII filters for checkpoint payloads.
next_steps: Engineer spike: implement minimal server-side checkpoint store and resume acceptance logic (2 sprints)
SDK prototypes: JS + Python with atomicAction helper API (1 sprint)
Internal dogfood: integrate with search-indexing example and mobile client with flaky network
Telemetry: wire event export and build per-session cost/latency dashboard query
notes_to_reviewers: Looking for feedback on: 1) the APIs ergonomics (are start/commit/abort verbs intuitive?), 2) checkpoint frequency defaults, and 3) security model for resumable tokens in our hosted plans. Please annotate with thumbs-up/thumbs-down on the Confluence PR and add technical comments on the GitHub prototype when ready.
